articles.title: Japanese consortium plans ammonia supply chain and car carrier fleet
articles.summary: Seven Japanese companies have agreed to develop an integrated ammonia fuel supply chain and introduce four ammonia-fuelled car carriers. The project brings together Imabari Shipbuilding, Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (“K” Line), Kyokuyo Shipyard, JERA, Shin Kurushima Dockyard, Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK) and Nihon...
articles.body: Seven Japanese companies have agreed to develop an integrated ammonia fuel supply chain and introduce four ammonia-fuelled car carriers. The project brings together Imabari Shipbuilding, Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (“K” Line), Kyokuyo Shipyard, JERA, Shin Kurushima Dockyard, Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK) and Nihon Shipyard. The partners described the initiative as the world’s first commercial project to integrate green ammonia procurement, loading infrastructure, ship-to-ship bunkering and vessel operations. Chubu region to become ammonia supply hub The project will use Japan’s Chubu region as its central hub. JERA will procure green ammonia from markets including India and develop new loading facilities at the ammonia terminal next to the Hekinan Thermal Power Station. The infrastructure will supply a dedicated ammonia bunkering vessel. Kyokuyo Shipyard will design and build the vessel, which is scheduled for completion in 2030. NYK or one of its wholly owned subsidiaries will own and operate the bunkering vessel. “K” Line and NYK will also establish an equally owned joint venture. The new company will sell and supply ammonia fuel through ship-to-ship bunkering, primarily at the ports of Nagoya and Mikawa. Four ammonia-fuelled car carriers “K” Line and NYK will each introduce two ammonia-fuelled car carriers. All four vessels are scheduled for completion in 2030. The ships are expected to transport finished vehicles for customers including Toyota Motor Corporation. According to the partners, they will be Japan’s first ammonia-fuelled car carriers. Each vessel will feature a dual-fuel engine capable of using ammonia. The ships will also have enough ammonia storage capacity to complete trans-Pacific voyages using the fuel alone. Shin Kurushima Dockyard will lead the basic design work. It will then work with Imabari Shipbuilding and Nihon Shipyard on the detailed design and construction of the vessels. Safety measures for ammonia operations Ammonia produces no carbon dioxide when combusted. However, its toxicity and corrosive properties require dedicated safety systems. The car carriers will therefore include several layers of protection. These will cover leak prevention, detection and ammonia neutralisation. The bunkering vessel will also feature specialised equipment designed to prevent leaks and support the safe transfer of ammonia fuel. Through the project, the companies aim to establish a stable ammonia supply system for international shipping. They also intend to support the development of a wider low-carbon ammonia market.

articles.summary: Hanwha Defense USA is moving to take control of Hanwha Philly Shipyard, bringing the Philadelphia facility under its U.S. defense business as the South Korean conglomerate pushes to expand into...

Photo courtesy Hanwha Philly Shipyard Hanwha Defense USA is moving to take control of Hanwha Philly Shipyard, bringing the Philadelphia facility under its U.S. defense business as the South Korean conglomerate pushes to expand into American naval shipbuilding. The company announced Tuesday that it will acquire a controlling 60% stake in the shipyard through an HDUSA-led joint venture, a restructuring intended to align Hanwha’s commercial and government shipbuilding operations under a single leadership structure. The move does not represent a new acquisition by Hanwha Group, which purchased the former Philly Shipyard for $100 million in December 2024. Instead, it transfers control from Hanwha Systems, which currently holds 60% of the shipyard, to Hanwha Defense USA Shipbuilding LLC, a joint venture between HDUSA and Hanwha FutureProof. Hanwha Ocean will retain its 40% stake. According to a September regulatory filing in South Korea, the transaction is valued at approximately $237.6 million, with completion planned for October 31. Retired Rear Adm. Tom Anderson, president of U.S. shipbuilding at HDUSA, will oversee the company’s American shipbuilding operations. “As Hanwha Defense USA continues to grow its multi-domain presence across the U.S., bringing the Philly Shipyard under HDUSA will further align our government and commercial shipbuilding efforts,” said Michael Coulter, president and CEO of Hanwha Defense USA. “We look forward to continuing to invest in our Philly Shipyard facilities and workforce in preparation for exciting work ahead.” The restructuring is the latest step in a transformation that began years before Hanwha acquired the yard. In 2019, Philly Shipyard faced an uncertain future after delivering the last of two containerships to Matson, leaving its commercial newbuilding orderbook empty. With no new construction contracts, the shipyard’s workforce had fallen from approximately 1,200 employees at the beginning of 2018 to just 80 by July 2019. The yard turned to government work to survive, adopting what was then described as a strategy to “go gray.” Its first contracts involved maintenance and repair work on the Maritime Administration’s Ready Reserve Force ships FSS Antares and FSS Pollux , allowing it to recall some laid-off workers and put its drydocks back to use. Those early contracts helped bridge the gap, but the real turning point came in April 2020, when Philly Shipyard was selected to construct the first two National Security Multi-Mission Vessels (NSMVs) under a $630 million contract managed by TOTE Services. The program eventually expanded to five ships, providing the long-term production backlog needed to rebuild the workforce. The yard continued pursuing government repair work, including a 2021 contract for the Military Sealift Command’s USNS Charlton . Now, seven years after that initial shift toward government work, Hanwha is preparing to take the next step, positioning the facility to build vessels directly for the U.S. Navy. In August 2025, Hanwha announced plans to invest $5 billion in the shipyard , including additional dry docks, expanded waterfront facilities and modernized production capabilities. The long-term goal is to increase annual production capacity to as many as 20 vessels. Hanwha said in September that the shipyard’s workforce had more than doubled since its acquisition, reaching nearly 2,500 employees. The yard now has a substantial commercial orderbook, including three LNG-powered containerships for Matson, two LNG carriers for Hanwha Shipping and four firm medium-range tanker orders, with options for six additional vessels. It has also delivered four of five NSMVs for MARAD, with the fifth scheduled for delivery in 2027. More recently, Hanwha secured another federal shipbuilding program. Earlier this month, TOTE Services finalized a contract with MARAD to manage construction of the first of a new generation of Missile Range Instrumentation Vessels for the U.S. Missile Defense Agency, awarding the shipbuilding subcontract to Hanwha Philly Shipyard. The first vessel, Golden Defender , is scheduled for delivery in 2030. The program builds on the existing NSMV production line, with the new missile-tracking vessels sharing approximately 70% design commonality with the training ships. While that contract represents another step into defense-related shipbuilding, Hanwha’s larger ambition is to establish Philadelphia as a shipyard capable of constructing vessels directly for the U.S. Navy. That effort received high-level attention in September when Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao toured the facility and met with Hanwha executives to discuss shipbuilding capacity, workforce development and future Navy requirements. “Over the past two years Hanwha has made significant investments in the Philly Shipyard to contribute to the revitalization of the U.S. shipbuilding industry,” Anderson said. “Now we are positioning the shipyard to transition to dual-use, aligning shipyard operations, workforce, and customer relations in preparation to build for the U.S. Navy, other federal agencies, and commercial customers.” For a shipyard that was struggling to find work just seven years ago, the announcement marks another milestone in its transformation from a commercial shipbuilder into a potential supplier for the U.S. defense industrial base. articles.body: Cabling October 27, 2026 · 8 hours ago Fugro wins UXO survey contract for German offshore grid connections 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Fugro Fugro has been awarded a contract by 50Hertz to deliver unexploded ordnance (UXO) survey, identification and clearance services for the LanWin3 and LanWin6 offshore grid connection projects in the German sector of the North Sea. By identifying and addressing potential hazards, the work will help 50Hertz prepare the routes for the safe installation of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables connecting offshore wind farms to Germany’s electricity network. LanWin3 and LanWin6 form part of Germany’s ongoing expansion of its offshore wind energy infrastructure. Once completed, each grid connection is designed to transmit up to 2 GW of offshore wind power, providing a combined transmission capacity of 4 GW and helping bring more renewable electricity from the North Sea into the national grid to build energy security and meet climate targets. Starting in the second quarter of 2027, the UXO survey will cover 200-meter-wide corridors along the LanWin3 and LanWin6 routes. The work will be carried out using two Geowing systems, Fugro's fixed magnetic gradiometer arrays, each fitted with ten magnetic sensors to detect potential UXO and other objects on or beneath the seabed. The survey will provide the geo-data needed to map potential targets and create a master target list for further investigation. Follow-on inspection and identification activities will take place in 2028, using remotely operated vehicle (ROV) technology and specialist detection systems to investigate selected targets and remove debris where required. Fugro will also support the safe removal and disposal of any confirmed UXO in accordance with regulatory requirements, helping prepare the cable corridors for installation. "On a project of this scale, the challenge is that the number and nature of potential UXO can only be known once the survey is complete. Building a reliable picture of the seabed at an early stage will allow 50Hertz to plan the next steps with greater certainty and manage safety throughout the cable installation programme," said Ronny Bøhn, Fugro’s Director of Marine Geophysics for Europe and Africa. articles.summary: Seatrium announced that it has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with global floating power solutions specialist Karpowership to pursue a joint venture to develop floating power and infrastructure solutions in Singapore, with…
articles.body: Seatrium, Karpowership Link Up on Floating Power and Digital Infrastructure Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 27, 2026 © Seatrium Seatrium announced that it has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with global floating power solutions specialist Karpowership to pursue a joint venture to develop floating power and infrastructure solutions in Singapore, with the potential to extend cooperation to the wider Southeast Asia market. The two companies will create an integrated platform combining infrastructure development, financing, engineering, construction and operations. The collaboration brings together Seatrium’s global offshore engineering, procurement and construction and systems integration capabilities with Karpowership’s expertise in developing, financing, owning and operating floating power and digital infrastructure, alongside its experience in delivering behind-the-meter power solutions for super intelligence. Announced at Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026 and witnessed by Dr. Tan See Leng, Singapore’s Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry), the MoU establishes a framework to jointly develop rapidly deployable power and infrastructure solutions in Singapore, which may include Powerships, floating data centers, turbine-based or hybrid vessels and floating nuclear solutions. The partners share a longer-term ambition to bolster Singapore’s position to serve as a resilient regional hub for rapidly deployable energy and digital infrastructure solutions. Today, Singapore remains heavily reliant on imported natural gas, which accounts for approximately 95% of its electricity generation, according to the Energy Market Authority. Continued disruptions to global fuel supplies have reinforced the need for diversifying energy sources and strengthening the resilience of Singapore's electricity system. At the same time, EMA estimates that Singapore's peak electricity demand is projected to grow between 2.4% and 4.8% annually to reach up to 11.4 gigawatts by 2031, driven in part by transport electrification and the expansion of energy-intensive industries on the island, including semiconductor manufacturing and data centres. Across Southeast Asia, the similar growth of digital industries has also led to increased infrastructure requirements. According to the 9 th ASEAN Energy Outlook, 20% of ASEAN's projected electricity demand growth in the next five years will be attributable to data centres. This, compounded with structural drivers of industrialisation and urbanisation, emphasise the need for reliable power to support industrial activity and other energy-intensive facilities. Against this backdrop, floating power infrastructure could provide additional options to enhance supply security, including through the rapid deployment of generation capacity, contingency power provision and support for critical infrastructure, including data centers. Such solutions, including the potential use of emerging energies such as hydrogen, could also offer flexibility in deployment locations, enable power generation assets to be adapted or redeployed, and chart a longer-term transition pathway as energy requirements continue to evolve. This MoU represents a new phase in the companies’ relationship. Since 2018, Seatrium has delivered seven FSRU conversions to Karpowership, with the 8 th and 9 th unit awarded this year, supporting the deployment of Karpowership’s LNG-to-power solutions across international markets. Seatrium has most recently secured a contract in October for the development and integration of Karpowership’s hydrogen-ready third-generation Whale Class Powerships to be deployed in countries requiring reliable energy supply.

articles.title: ANYbotics Delivers Explosion-Protected Inspection Robots for Offshore Energy
articles.summary: Swiss robotics company ANYbotics has begun customer deliveries of ANYmal X, a four-legged autonomous inspection robot designed to operate in potentially explosive environments, opening new opportunities for robotic inspection across offshore…
articles.body: ANYbotics Delivers Explosion-Protected Inspection Robots for Offshore Energy Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 27, 2026 Image courtesy ANYbotics Image courtesy ANYbotics Swiss robotics company ANYbotics has begun customer deliveries of ANYmal X, a four-legged autonomous inspection robot designed to operate in potentially explosive environments, opening new opportunities for robotic inspection across offshore oil and gas installations and industrial processing facilities. Initial customers include Equinor and DSM-Firmenich , following an extensive testing program involving BP, Shell, PETRONAS, Petrobras, BASF and SLB . Since 2023, participating companies have evaluated the technology across hundreds of onshore and offshore inspection missions. ANYmal X is engineered to meet ATEX and IECEx explosion-protection standards, addressing a major obstacle to deploying autonomous mobile robots in hazardous areas containing flammable gases or vapors. The robot navigates stairs, narrow walkways and complex industrial infrastructure without requiring facility modifications. Integrated thermal, visual, acoustic and gas sensors monitor pumps, compressors, valves and piping for overheating, leaks, abnormal noise and equipment deterioration. "Many experts thought a legged robot could never be made safe for explosive atmospheres," said Péter Fankhauser, Co-Founder and CEO of ANYbotics . "That changes today." Developing the system required four years of engineering and resulted in more than 10 patents, according to the company. Explosion-protection measures include nitrogen-filled sealed chambers housing electronics and inspection equipment, flameproof enclosures protecting the battery and 12 leg actuators, conductive feet for grounding and automatic temperature monitoring. ANYmal X operates through ANYbotics' Shift platform, which schedules autonomous inspection rounds, associates collected measurements with individual assets and integrates findings into existing maintenance management systems, including SAP, Yokogawa and SLB platforms. The technology is intended to reduce personnel exposure to hazardous operating environments while providing repeatable equipment condition data for predictive maintenance and digital twin applications. ANYbotics reports that its existing industrial inspection systems conduct more than 120,000 autonomous inspections monthly across over 50 customers in power, metals and materials industries. The company will publicly demonstrate ANYmal X and its industrial AI platform alongside SLB and Kuwait Oil Company at ADIPEC 2026, November 2–5, in Abu Dhabi. Image courtesy ANYbotics

articles.title: Norway Grants Funding to Advance Nuclear Propulsion for Ships
articles.summary: The Research Council of Norway has awarded $2 million (NOK 20 million) in initial funding to the Emerald Nuclear Norway-led Marine Nuclear Propulsion System (MarNuPS) project, which aims to develop and test an integrated nuclear propulsion system for offshore vessels…
articles.body: Norway Grants Funding to Advance Nuclear Propulsion for Ships Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. October 27, 2026 (Credit: Emerald Nuclear Norway) The Research Council of Norway has awarded $2 million (NOK 20 million) in initial funding to the Emerald Nuclear Norway-led Marine Nuclear Propulsion System (MarNuPS) project, which aims to develop and test an integrated nuclear propulsion system for offshore vessels, with first deployment targeted for 2031-32. The project brings together Emerald Nuclear Norway, VARD Group, Vard Electro, Island Offshore, NTNU, Imperial College London and Maskindynamikk to advance maritime nuclear propulsion from system development towards physical integration and testing. The funding comes alongside substantial investment from the project partners, with the first stage of the program estimated to cost around $15. 6 million (NOK 150 million). MarNuPS will integrate Emerald Nuclear's 5 MWe Gem Microreactor technology with energy storage, power conversion, vessel power management, automation and bridge control systems. The first stage, planned for 2027, will involve establishing an integrated test facility at Stette, outside Ålesund, where a full-scale representation of the shipboard propulsion system will be assembled and tested. The facility will use electric heating instead of nuclear fuel, allowing the project partners to evaluate how the different systems operate together under conditions representative of vessel operations. Testing will cover normal operations, rapid changes in power demand, transient and stress conditions, system performance and crew interaction. “The partners are already making a substantial commitment to MarNuPS, and this support gives the programme additional backing as we move from design and analysis towards building and testing a complete integrated system. It's only the beginning of a longer development and qualification process, but it demonstrates that maritime nuclear propulsion is now being pursued as a serious industrial project,” said Hallgeir Juliebø, Co-Founder and Chief Commercial Officer of Emerald Nuclear and Chairman of Emerald Nuclear Norway. Emerald Nuclear's Gem Microreactor is designed for ships and floating remote-power applications. Under the company's proposed leasing model, Emerald Nuclear would retain ownership and operation of the reactor and responsibility for the fuel cycle, while shipowners would purchase the power. Island Offshore plans to become the first shipowner to install the reactor and energy system, with deployment targeted for 2031-32. “Nuclear energy has the potential to provide a new route to decarbonizing offshore vessels without compromising the power, endurance and operational flexibility these ships require,” added Tommy Walaunet, CEO of Island Offshore. The project partners will contribute expertise across reactor technology, ship design, power management, vessel operations, nuclear modelling, structural integrity and condition monitoring. MarNuPS builds on earlier Norwegian research into maritime nuclear propulsion, including the NTNU-led NuProShip program, and forms part of the demonstration work linked to SFI SAINT national research center.

articles.title: Accelerating operational excellence in offshore energy
articles.summary: By- Nisha Lathif, General Manager, Oil and Gas,Honeywell Technologies With decades of expertise in addressing the complex needs of the energy...
articles.body: Branded Content October 27, 2026 · 9 hours ago Accelerating operational excellence in offshore energy Written in partnership with Honeywell Technologies 6 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Integrated offshore solutions by Honeywell Technologies @Honeywell Technologies By- Nisha Lathif, General Manager, Oil and Gas,Honeywell Technologies With decades of expertise in addressing the complex needs of the energy sector in challenging marine environments, Honeywell Technologies is at the heart of shaping the future of offshore energy operations. Our advances are supporting a fundamental shift in the industry, helping transform traditional offshore operations into becoming more connected, intelligent and data driven. As digital technologies continue to evolve, we see that operators can leverage real-time data, advanced analytics and integrated operational platforms to gain deeper insights into asset performance and operational efficiency. This shift is enabling organizations to make more informed decisions, optimize maintenance and production strategies and create more agile, resilient offshore operations. Offshore operations are entering a new era Offshore energy operators are confronting a convergence of pressures that traditional ways of working were never designed to handle. Aging infrastructure is becoming a primary constraint today. While equipment ages, operational complexity continues to increase, experienced offshore professionals are becoming harder to replace and the pressure to improve reliability and safety while managing costs remains high. 4,5 The key to solving many of these challenges can be found in data. Modern offshore facilities generate massive volumes of operational data. Historically, much of this information was underutilized, trapped in individual systems or available only after issues had already occurred. Some operators are now moving beyond traditional maintenance strategies to embrace digital technologies that enable smarter, faster operational decision-making. The organizations making the greatest progress are those that convert operational data into actionable intelligence. Rather than simply collecting information, they are using analytics and connected systems to identify risks earlier, optimize maintenance activities and improve operational performance before failures impact production. Why predictive operations matter Reactive and time-based maintenance have clear limitations. Waiting for equipment to fail means unplanned downtime, lost production and elevated safety risk. Servicing equipment on a fixed calendar schedule, regardless of actual condition, wastes resources and can compromise assets through unnecessary intervention. Condition-based maintenance (CBM) offers a proactive alternative, focusing on real-time monitoring rather than adherence to fixed schedules. Operational and equipment data are continuously monitored to assess actual asset health. By combining real-time monitoring with advanced analytics, operators can identify emerging issues before they develop into significant failures. The benefits of this approach are substantial: · Reduced unplanned downtime · Better maintenance prioritization · Improved equipment availability · Reduced operational risk · Enhanced workforce productivity By assessing the actual state of equipment, operators can conduct maintenance only when conditions warrant it, effectively reducing unnecessary downtime and optimizing resource allocation. CBM moves beyond simple data collection. When data, analytics and human expertise are connected, operators gain the ability to move from reacting to problems toward anticipating and preventing them. That helps people make faster, better decisions. Aker BP: A case study of CBM in offshore operations 2, 3 Aker BP, a leading energy exploration and production company operating on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, offers a practical illustration of CBM in action. Like many offshore producers, their challenges included managing equipment reliability and conducting maintenance across multiple offshore assets while maintaining high safety standards and operational efficiency. To overcome these challenges Aker BP adopted condition-based maintenance using Honeywell Technologies Forge Asset Performance Management (APM), a connected platform that integrates real-time data from multiple equipment types and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) into a single dashboard, creating a unified, OEM-agnostic approach to asset health monitoring that facilitates proactive decision-making. With Honeywell Technologies Forge APM now providing enterprise-wide control, Aker BP can continuously monitor equipment conditions on six of its assets in the North Sea, ensuring that maintenance is carried out only when necessary. Aker BP reports that the real benefits of using CBM strategies have been meaningful: · Earlier identification of equipment issues · Reduced dependence on manual inspections · Better prioritization of maintenance activities · Improved situational awareness In addition, equipment essential for safety—such as safety valves, pressure sensors and critical control systems — receives focused attention based on its operational status. The new approach also carries clear safety benefits for Aker BP. By reducing the frequency of scheduled maintenance (some of it unnecessary), CBM minimizes disruptions to their ongoing operations, thereby decreasing the chances of accidents during maintenance activities. The advantages gained were not simply from software deployment. Dedicated ownership and continuous refinement were also essential. Experienced technicians at Aker BP set up their own models in the system specifically for their required calculations. They engaged ongoing improvement and adaptation to the monitoring process that allowed engineers to tune the system more effectively, minimize false alerts and concentrate on critical issues. This is a reminder that predictive maintenance is fundamentally a new operating model. Success requires connected data, advanced analytics and experienced personnel working together to make better decisions. Technology provides visibility and insight, but operational excellence still depends on informed human judgment. Lessons for the offshore industry The Aker BP experience points to several broader ideals for the offshore industry: · Connect data across systems. Operators need a unified view instead of isolated monitoring tools. Integrating data from multiple equipment types and OEMs into a single dashboard enables proactive decision-making. · Focus on actionable insights. The goal is not more alerts—the goal is better decisions. Minimizing false alerts keeps attention on critical issues. · Combine technology and expertise . Analytics support engineers, but people remain central to decision-making. · Create a culture of continuous improvement. Condition-monitoring systems become more valuable as teams refine models and operating practices over time. Building the offshore operation of the future Putting these ideals into practice to create future-ready offshore operations requires an integrated operating environment that connects production systems, assets, people, safety functions and sustainability objectives. Honeywell Technologies engages in all aspects of transforming offshore operations through six connected domains that collectively support safer, more efficient and more resilient offshore production. For the operational foundation we bring operations and control capabilities, including SCADA, process control, telemetry and connectivity that provide visibility across offshore assets. We enable digital transformation technologies such as Industrial IoT, predictive analytics, AI-enabled operations and digital twins to help organizations transform data into operational intelligence. Honeywell Technologies asset performance solutions support reliability and optimization through asset performance management platforms, turbomachinery optimization, measurement technologies and energy management capabilities. Our people and collaboration technologies enable remote operations, expert collaboration, knowledge management and workforce training, addressing the growing workforce challenges across offshore operations. Our safety and security systems integrate process safety, cybersecurity, and fire and gas systems into a unified operational environment. We compliment these with sustainability solutions that incorporate emissions monitoring, energy optimization and carbon management capabilities. The entire portfolio of Honeywell Technologies’ offshore production capabilities creates a connected operational ecosystem where data flows across functions, enabling faster decisions, improved efficiency and greater resilience. The next frontier of operational excellence As the Aker BP example demonstrates, the real value of offshore operational excellence lies not in technology alone, but in transforming operational data into actionable insights. By connecting assets, people and processes within a unified operational environment, operators can improve reliability, enhance efficiency and support safer operations. As the industry evolves, condition-based maintenance and predictive analytics will continue to play a key role in building more resilient and high-performing offshore operations. articles.body: Exploration & Production October 27, 2026 · 9 hours ago Go-ahead for North Sea wildcat clears path for Equinor’s drilling ops with COSL rig Norwegian authorities have approved a new hydrocarbon exploration well, continuing the country's active drilling program. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 1 minutes read LinkedIn X Email COSL Promoter rig Source: COSL Drilling Europe Norway’s energy giant Equinor has secured the green light to drill an exploration well in the North Sea, using one of COSL Drilling Europe’s semi-submersible rigs. The Norwegian Offshore Directorate has granted Equinor a drilling permit for the wellbore 33/9-F-4 DH in production license 1214 . This license, which was awarded on March 15, 2024, and is valid until the same date in 2030, is owned by Equinor (17%), Petoro (30%), OKEA (28%), and Vår Energi (25%). The drilling of the wildcat well will be carried out using the 2012-built COSL Promoter semi-submersible rig designed to operate in water depths up to 750 meters. This drilling permit comes months after the Norwegian Ocean Industry Authority (Havtil) gave Equinor consent to use the same semi-submersible rig for permanent plugging and abandonment (P&A) on the Tordis field. articles.title: Fugro to hunt for unexploded munitions along North Sea cable routes
articles.summary: Dutch survey specialist Fugro has secured a contract from German transmission system operator 50Hertz to survey and clear unexploded ordnance along the routes of two offshore wind grid connections in the North Sea. The contract covers the LanWin3 and LanWin6 high-voltage direct current links, each designed to...
articles.body: Europe Offshore Renewables Fugro to hunt for unexploded munitions along North Sea cable routes Bojan Lepic October 27, 2026 0 55 1 minute read Fugro Fugro Dutch survey specialist Fugro has secured a contract from German transmission system operator 50Hertz to survey and clear unexploded ordnance along the routes of two offshore wind grid connections in the North Sea. The contract covers the LanWin3 and LanWin6 high-voltage direct current links, each designed to transmit up to 2GW of offshore wind power to Germany’s electricity grid, providing a combined capacity of 4GW. Offshore surveys are scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027, covering 200 m-wide corridors along both cable routes. Fugro will deploy two Geowing magnetic gradiometer systems, each equipped with ten sensors, to detect potential unexploded munitions and other objects on or beneath the seabed. The resulting data will identify targets requiring further investigation before cable installation. Follow-up activities in 2028 will include remotely operated vehicle inspections, identification of suspicious objects, and debris removal. Fugro will also support the clearance and disposal of confirmed unexploded ordnance. Ronny Bøhn, Fugro’s director of marine geophysics for Europe and Africa, said early seabed investigations would help 50Hertz better understand potential hazards and manage risks throughout the cable installation programme. articles.body: Maersk has announced revised Peak Season Surcharges (PSS) for shipments from Asia to destinations in Southern and East Africa. The new rates will take effect in November 2026 and remain applicable until further notice. Far East Asia to South Africa and Mauritius The revised PSS will apply from 9 November 2026. For shipments originating in Vietnam, it will take effect on 10 November. The origin scope includes China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. Destination All 20-foot containers All 40-foot containers South Africa and Mauritius US$1,000 US$2,000 China and Hong Kong to East Africa Maersk will also increase the PSS from China and Hong Kong to Kenya and Dar es Salaam from 9 November 2026. Destination All 20-foot containers All 40-foot containers All 45-foot containers Kenya US$1,000 US$2,000 US$2,000 Dar es Salaam US$1,200 US$2,000 US$2,000 For non-SPOT bookings, Maersk will determine the applicable rate using the Price Calculation Date (PCD). For non-FMC shipments, the PCD is the scheduled departure date of the first water leg shown when the booking is confirmed. For FMC shipments, the PCD is the final container gate-in date. For SPOT bookings, the applicable rate will be based on the booking confirmation date or the first vessel’s estimated departure date at booking confirmation. The surcharge will be collected at origin unless customers select different payment terms. Other local and contingency charges may also apply.

articles.body: Vessels & Vehicles October 27, 2026 · 9 hours ago Former IMR ship strengthens Asso.subsea's fleet as trenching support vessel NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 1 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Asso.subsea via LinkedIn Greece’s Asso.subsea has taken delivery of the new addition to its fleet, the trenching support vessel (TSV) Arete, previously the inspection, maintenance and repair (IMR) vessel Viking Reach. It was reported in August that Asso.subsea was buying Viking Reach from Eidesvik Reach, in which Eidesvik holds a 50.1% ownership interest and Reach Subsea 49.9%, with plans on renaming it to Arete. The vessel was delivered to the Greek company yesterday, October 26. "Named after the revered Queen of the Phaeacians from Greek mythology, a figure synonymous with wisdom, noble leadership, and providing safe harbor, TSV Arete embodies our continued commitment to excellence and reliability in marine operations," Asso.subsea said on social media. With its high-capacity subsea equipment, 70-ton AHC crane, integrated work-class remotely operated vehicle (WROV) and survey spreads, shallow water capability and extensive deck area, Arete is described as “an extremely flexible asset” , equipped for multi-purpose roles in subsea cable protection, route preparation, post-lay burial, and the offshore wind market. The vessel, which will hoist the Greek flag, follows the newbuild orders of the TSVs Avra and Andromeda. articles.summary: US offshore services giant Chouest Group has acquired Canadian marine and offshore services provider Horizon Maritime, expanding its presence across Canada’s east and west coasts and into the Arctic. articles.body: Americas Offshore Chouest Group acquires Canada’s Horizon Maritime Bojan Lepic October 27, 2026 0 109 1 minute read Horizon Maritime Horizon Maritime US offshore services giant Chouest Group has acquired Canadian marine and offshore services provider Horizon Maritime, expanding its presence across Canada’s east and west coasts and into the Arctic. The Louisiana-based group has partnered with Horizon Maritime’s founders to acquire the St. John’s-headquartered company from CFFI and its lender HPS. The transaction’s financial details were not disclosed. The acquisition combines Chouest’s global offshore support fleet, subsea services, shipbuilding, specialised engineering, and marine technology capabilities with Horizon’s operations in Canada’s offshore energy and harsh-environment markets. The companies said the combination would let Horizon expand across all three Canadian coastlines, giving customers access to a broader range of marine transportation, subsea, and offshore services. Horizon Maritime will retain its existing management and leadership structure, with Steve Widmeyer continuing as chief executive. Widmeyer and company co-founder Sean Leet will also join the board of directors. Founded in 2015, Horizon Maritime operates in offshore energy, Arctic logistics, and specialised marine services. Its fleet includes the anchor-handling tug supply vessel Horizon Arctic , the platform supply vessel Horizon Dragon , and the icebreaker Polar Prince , along with three smaller utility tugs designed for operations in icy waters. The company also operates a Canadian harbour towage joint venture with Dutch towage specialist Kotug, established in 2019. articles.title: Eni locks in offshore contractors for Cyprus gas project
articles.summary: Italian energy major Eni has signed the main engineering, procurement, construction, and drilling contracts for the Cronos gas development offshore Cyprus, with a string of major offshore contractors securing work on the project. The contracts, valued by local media at around $1.8bn, mark the start of the...
articles.body: Europe Offshore Eni locks in offshore contractors for Cyprus gas project Bojan Lepic October 27, 2026 0 98 1 minute read Eni Eni Italian energy major Eni has signed the main engineering, procurement, construction, and drilling contracts for the Cronos gas development offshore Cyprus, with a string of major offshore contractors securing work on the project. The contracts, valued by local media at around $1.8bn, mark the start of the development’s execution phase in Block 6, following a final investment decision by Eni and partner TotalEnergies in July. Although Eni did not disclose the contractors involved, local media identified eight companies awarded work on the development, covering subsea production systems, pipelines, offshore installation, drilling and associated infrastructure. Baker Hughes will design, procure, and construct subsea production systems, while TechnipFMC will supply flexible gas production lines. Dalmine has been selected to supply gas export and monoethylene glycol pipelines, with Oceaneering International responsible for subsea umbilicals and control systems. China Merchants Heavy Industry will design, construct, transport, and install a floating control unit. US offshore engineering contractor McDermott will handle offshore transportation, installation, tie-ins, and commissioning of subsea pipelines and equipment. McDermott had already announced a contract worth between $500m and $750m for Cronos in September, marking its first subsea project award from Eni. Egyptian contractor Petrojet will construct a new onshore gas pipeline connecting the Zohr facilities with the Damietta LNG terminal, while Italy’s Saipem has been selected to provide drilling services using its Saipem 10000 drillship. Separately, Halliburton secured a bundled well construction and completions contract for Cronos in September, covering drilling fluids, directional drilling, cementing, automation, and other well services. The Cronos development will involve four subsea wells targeting resources estimated at more than 3trn cubic feet of gas initially in place. Production is expected to begin in the first half of 2028, reaching a plateau of up to 500m standard cubic feet per day. Gas will be transported to Egypt for processing through existing Zohr-field infrastructure before being liquefied at Damietta for export, primarily to European markets. Eni operates Block 6 with a 50% stake, while TotalEnergies holds the remaining interest. articles.summary: Oman’s Asyad Group has priced an institutional share sale in its listed shipping subsidiary at OMR50.8m ($132m), reducing its ownership as part of a move to broaden the company’s shareholder base. Muscat-listed Asyad Shipping said the institutional bookbuilding process closed heavily oversubscribed. The transaction...
articles.body: Middle East Operations Asyad Group prices $132m shipping stake sale Adis Ajdin October 27, 2026 0 149 1 minute read Asyad Shipping Asyad Shipping Oman’s Asyad Group has priced an institutional share sale in its listed shipping subsidiary at OMR50.8m ($132m), reducing its ownership as part of a move to broaden the company’s shareholder base. Muscat-listed Asyad Shipping said the institutional bookbuilding process closed heavily oversubscribed. The transaction covers 5% of Asyad Shipping’s issued share capital. Upon completion, the company’s free float will rise to 25%, meeting the minimum requirement set by Oman’s Financial Services Authority. The shares are being sold by parent Asyad Group, which will receive the proceeds. No new shares are being issued, and Asyad Shipping will not receive any of the funds. The group is also preparing a separate retail offering of up to 1.25% of the shipping company at the same price, subject to regulatory approval. Settlement and listing of the institutional shares are expected on November 4. The remaining shares held by Asyad Group will be subject to a 180-day lock-up following settlement. The transaction follows Asyad Shipping’s March 2025 initial public offering, which raised approximately $333m and brought 20% of the company into public ownership. Since listing, the company has continued expanding and renewing its fleet across the tanker, dry bulk, gas and container sectors. Asyad operated a fleet of 91 vessels at the end of June, including 48 owned or co-owned ships, 31 chartered-in vessels and 12 newbuildings. Its latest investment programme includes eight charter-backed MR product tankers ordered at HD Hyundai and three VLCCs contracted at Hanwha Ocean earlier this year. The company has also been recycling capital through secondhand sales. In September, it agreed to dispose of three ageing tankers for a combined OMR68.44m ($178m), including two VLCCs. articles.title: Dolphin Drilling parts ways with 52-year-old rig and forges pact with SPM
articles.summary: Dolphin Drilling has sealed a deal to divest its 1974-built rig for up to $25 million and formed a strategic partnership with SPM.
articles.body: Business & Finance October 27, 2026 · 11 hours ago Dolphin Drilling parts ways with 52-year-old rig and forges pact with SPM Dolphin Drilling has sealed a deal to divest its 1974-built rig for up to $25 million and formed a strategic partnership with SPM. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 4 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Blackford Dolphin rig; Source: Dolphin Drilling Dolphin Drilling, an Oslo-listed, Aberdeen-headquartered owner and operator of a fleet of harsh-environment mid-water and deepwater semi-submersible drilling rigs, has taken a step to strengthen its financial position, offloading its semi-submersible rig for $25 million in a transaction expected to close next month in Singapore, while partnering with SPM Energy Shipping FZCO to capture upside in a tightening global rig market. Dolphin Drilling has entered into a definitive sale and purchase agreement (SPA) for the sale of the 1974-built Blackford Dolphin semi-submersible rig with SPM for a total consideration of $25 million, comprising $10 million, payable upon delivery of the rig and $15 million, payable when SPM receives the first payment under a potential future drilling contract. The sale is expected to close on or about November 5, 2026, in Singapore, immediately and materially reducing the firm’s operating cost base, eliminating the class renewal survey capital expenditures related to this rig and significantly strengthening the company’s financial position. The duo has also entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the management of future drilling contracts for this rig and one additional semi-submersible, as well as any other rigs or units that the two companies may agree upon. The company explains that these management arrangements contemplate entry into management agreements and other deals, which remain subject to definitive documentation and customary closing conditions. The contemplated management arrangements combine Dolphin Drilling’s established operating platform, technical expertise and long track record with the strong commercial presence of the participating companies in India and the surrounding regions. The rigs will be marketed by SPM in India and other areas agreed upon between the two players, with capital costs, operational expenses and guarantees related to future drilling contracts to be covered by SPM as owners of the rigs. Ronny Bjørnådal , Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dolphin Drilling, commented: “Dolphin Drilling will through the sale and contemplated management arrangements materially de-risk the company and at the same time, significantly reduce operating costs as well as eliminate capital expenditures associated with the class renewal survey for the Blackford Dolphin. “The transactions provide for potential future upside through management of Blackford Dolphin and one or more additional semi-submersible drilling rig resulting in future management fees and ability to grow our platform.” Related Articles Fossil Energy Dolphin Drilling: GHL cash-and-rig proposal ‘encouraging’ but settlement offer falls short 2 min read Dolphin Drilling believes the sale and management arrangements offer a compelling combination of immediate risk reduction and value realization while preserving exposure to the potential upside from improving offshore drilling market fundamentals and a further tightening of the supply and demand balance. The transactions are highly attractive to the company, as they are expected to reduce the company’s interest-bearing debt and its capital expenditures related to Blackford Dolphin while creating opportunities for future revenue generation from the semi-submersible and other rigs under management, complementing the firm’s existing operating model with capital-light revenue streams. Bjørnådal emphasized: “The management arrangements would combine SPM’s commercial capabilities, market access and relationships in some of the most active benign-water markets in the world with Dolphin Drilling’s established operating platform, technical expertise and worldwide operating licenses, a proven operating platform and decades of experience. “This gives us the flexibility to capture the prospective upside of a tightening rig market, while strengthening our platform and driving long-term shareholder value.” The strategic partnership aligns well with Dolphin Drilling’s broader, ongoing evaluation of strategic initiatives and business opportunities to participate in industry consolidation and further growth. The company reported at the end of second quarter 2026 improved financial figures, including total cash of $55.1 million and a firm revenue contracted backlog of $556 million, with a further $446 million in options, resulting from multi-year contracts secured for Paul B. Loyd Jr. and Borgland Dolphin . Related Articles Fossil Energy UK oil & gas operator hires Dolphin Drilling’s rig on multimillion-dollar gig 2 min read The offshore drilling contractor underlines that its current contract backlog, combined with the sale of Blackford Dolphin and the potential management arrangements, further enhances its financial stability and long-term outlook. The firm underlines that it is well positioned to continue to evaluate and pursue strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing long-term shareholder value, including organic growth opportunities, following the sale of this rig and the strategic partnership with SPM and their marketing consultant Valiant Oil and Gas (VOG) through the management arrangements. Dolphin Drilling noted: “The market for semi-submersible drilling rigs, the segment in which Dolphin Drilling’s fleet operates, remains tight. Years of limited newbuild activity, combined with the retirement and scrapping of older units, have significantly reduced the available supply of moored floaters, and there is no newbuild pipeline to replenish the fleet. “At the same time, demand is supported by a renewed focus on energy security and increased investments in offshore developments, including in benign-water regions such as India, Southeast Asia, Mexico and West Africa. articles.title: Zijin Mining orders bulker pair for African mineral trade
articles.summary: Chinese mining giant Zijin Mining has returned to Shandong Xinneng Shipbuilding for two 3,000 dwt bulk carriers, expanding its dedicated mineral transport operation on Lake Tanganyika in eastern Africa. The latest contract follows an earlier order for four 2,000 dwt vessels at the same Chinese yard, which are now...
articles.body: Dry Cargo Greater China Shipyards Zijin Mining orders bulker pair for African mineral trade Adis Ajdin October 27, 2026 0 213 1 minute read Xinneng Shipbuilding Xinneng Shipbuilding Chinese mining giant Zijin Mining has returned to Shandong Xinneng Shipbuilding for two 3,000 dwt bulk carriers, expanding its dedicated mineral transport operation on Lake Tanganyika in eastern Africa. The latest contract follows an earlier order for four 2,000 dwt vessels at the same Chinese yard, which are now operating on the lake between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania. The new ships will be 50% larger than their predecessors, adding a combined 6,000 dwt to Zijin’s lake transport capacity. Contract value and delivery dates have not been disclosed. The investment forms part of Zijin’s efforts to establish an alternative export corridor for minerals from its operations in the DRC. The group’s existing shipping operation links Congolese cargoes with Kigoma in Tanzania, from where they can move towards the country’s Indian Ocean export infrastructure. Zijin’s first four lake bulkers were built through an arrangement that saw hull sections manufactured in China and assembled in Tanzania, overcoming the logistical challenges of building vessels for an African inland waterway. The company established the route to support its growing mining interests in central Africa and reduce dependence on existing overland transport connections. According to the National Grid's Notice to Mariners (NtM) issued on October 8, Blue Eclipse was scheduled to start the operations on October 22 and continue until November 10, subject to prevailing weather conditions and work progress. The environmental camera survey is being performed in the North Sea from the nearshore limit north of the Viking Link cable, northeast of Mablethorpe, Lincolnshire, and extending offshore to the UK/Netherlands border. The survey works shall provide seabed imagery along 193 selected 100m transects along the route. Blue Eclipse is being operated from a remote operations center (ROC) in Aberdeen.
